newsitem.title: GREECE: Dutch Foreign Minister calls for calm in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Foreign Minister calls for calm in Cyprus.

text.p: Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo called on Tuesday for calm on the divided island of Cyprus.
Van Mierlo also said that scheduled negotiations for Cyprus to join the European Union would not be easy.

"The talks for Cyprus's EU membership (scheduled for 1998) won't be easy. Both parties involved in Cyprus should refrain from action which will increase tension," Van Mierlo said after talks with Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos.
Van Mierlo is visiting EU capitals after the Netherlands took over the rotating EU presidency this month.
Tension has risen on the Mediterranean island in recent weeks after the Nicosia government announced it would deploy a Russian missile system.
Turkey threatened military action several times last week to stop deployment of the S-300 system which the Cypriot government says is purely defensive.
Installation of the S-300 would provide Cyprus with a strong weapon for striking Turkey's air superiority in the region.

Turkey invaded Cyprus in 1974 in response to an attempted coup, inspired by the then Greek military junta in Athens. Turkey has kept about 30,000 troops on the northern third of the island since, ostensibly to protect the Turkish community.
Greece has a military defence pact with Cyprus and has been working to coordinate defence strategies with the internationally recognised Greek Cypriot government.
"The Cyprus issue is deadlocked for many years," Van Mierlo said. "We have to come to a breakthrough."
